31 Four diagrams representing the electric field between two oppositely charged point charges are
shown.
Which diagram correctly shows the electric field lines?
A
B
+
–
+
–
C
D
+
–
+
–

hints: Notice the + charge on the left and the - charge on the right and check which way each arrowhead points at each charge.
Recall field lines must start on positive charge and end on negative charge, so they must point away from + and toward -.
Compare the straight outer lines and the upper and lower curved lines between the charges to find the diagram where every line goes from + to -.
walkthrough: Identify the charges: + point charge on the left, - point charge on the right.
State the rule: electric field direction is the force on a positive test charge, so lines leave + and enter - and never enter + or leave -.
Check the central horizontal line: it must point to the right, from + to -.
Check the curved lines joining the charges: both the upper and lower connectors must point from + on the left to - on the right.
Check the outer lines: to the left of + they must point left away from +, and to the right and above or below - they must point toward -.
Only the diagram with all arrows leaving + and entering - satisfies every check, with no reversed outer line or reversed loop. This is option A.

A.explanation: All lines leave the + charge and enter the - charge, with the central and curved lines going from + to - as required for a dipole.

B.explanation: The outer lines on the + side point into + and the outer lines on the - side point away from -, opposite to leaving + and entering -.

C.explanation: The upper curved line between the charges points from - to +, so it shows field entering + and leaving -, which is reversed.

D.explanation: The straight line on the + side points into + and the upper curved line points from - to +, violating the + to - direction rule.
